title: Smartsweep: per-tenant per-route batching & cache recommender with staged apply
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a recommender and safe-deployment pipeline ("Smartsweep") that generates per-customer and per-route batching/caching configuration suggestions, simulates impact, and applies changes via a staged canary with automated rollback triggers.

Background: We currently have coarse-grained defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching. Customers and routes vary widely in token distribution, tail latency sensitivity, and cost sensitivity. Manual rules (allowlists/denylists) are laborious and error-prone. We need an automated system that: segments tenants and routes by workload characteristics, proposes tier-aware config profiles, verifies via offline and live dry-runs, and performs safe staged apply/rollback with observability hooks.

Scope:
- Data ingestion: collect per-route/per-tenant telemetry (p50/p95 latency, tokens/request, sequence length histogram, cache hit rate, cost per token).
- Segmenter: workload classifier that assigns customers/routes to segments (eg. interactive-low-latency, batch-high-throughput, embedding-heavy).
- Recommender: map segments to config suggestions (batch window, max batch size, KV cache policy, cache TTLs, quantization hints).
- Safety plane: offline simulator (dry-run) + live canary orchestrator with automatic rollback criteria (latency, error rate, quality regression proxies).
- Controls: support allowlists/denylists and tier overrides (Free / Standard / Enterprise) with explicit opt-out flags.

Non-goals: Automatic model selection, cross-customer data sharing, complex model fine-tuning for quality evaluation (we rely on prompt/sample evaluation hooks).

Success metrics:
- Mean per-token compute cost reduction across canary cohort >= 12% without >5% p95 latency regression.
- Automated rollback correctly triggered when latency or error spikes exceed thresholds in >=95% simulated fault runs.
- Reduction in manual rule tickets (PM/SE) by 40% in Q2 after rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Recommender produces deterministic JSON suggestions for any customer+route input based on telemetry snapshot
Offline dry-run simulator can replay past 14 days of traffic and produce cost/latency delta report
Canary orchestrator can stage changes to 0.5%, 5%, 20% traffic buckets and automatically halt/rollback based on SLO breaches
Admin UI exposes allowlist/denylist and per-tier overrides and shows recommendation rationale
Audit log contains exact config diffs and rollout timeline for every apply
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive batching reduces cost but can increase p95 for interactive routes; we prioritize per-route SLO bindings over aggregate cost savings.
Decision: Start with conservative batch window defaults per segment and grow via staged percent increases tied to observed p95.
Edge-case: short-lived routes (bursty ephemeral APIs) will be labeled 'no-batching' by default via denylist heuristics unless explicitly allowed.
Privacy: recommender only uses aggregated telemetry and no request payloads; KMS keys used for storing audit metadata where required.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18 - Ticket created by Maya Chen: outlined scope and stakeholders (platform, runtime, console, SRE)
2025-02-24 - Spike completed: collected telemetry schema and identified 6 core features (tokens, seq_len_dist, p50/p95, cache_hit_rate, model_family, error_rate)
2025-02-28 - Prototype recommender implemented (rule-based mapping) and integrated with offline simulator; initial simulation on 3 customers showed ~9% cost reduction with 2% p95 regression
2025-03-03 - Canary controller integration PR ready; pairing session scheduled with SRE for rollback thresholds calibration
2025-03-05 - Safety checklist drafted; need PM sign-off for tier defaults and allow/deny semantics
review_feedback: PM (Anika Gupta): prefer explicit enterprise override and email notification for any auto-rollback affecting >1% traffic
Design (Ravi Patel): UI should show 'why' for each recommendation (top 3 contributing signals)
SRE (Laura Kim): require a 15min dry-window metric evaluation after each rollout stage before proceeding
open_questions: Should quality regressions use model-level eval sets or rely on proxy metrics (token-level perplexity, error rate) for initial rollout?
What is the TTL for recommendations before they are recomputed (24h vs 7d)?
How to prioritize conflicting suggestions when customer has manual overrides?
